review_notes: I read the whole file. Its main constructions (Equiv.map, Equiv.functor, Equiv.traverse, Equiv.traversable) are already exposed as Functor and Traversable structures. The lawfulness proofs are bundled in Equiv.lawfulFunctor and Equiv.isLawfulTraversable. The loose facts (id_map, comp_map, id_traverse, comp_traverse, naturality and similar) are the fields of those lawful classes, and they are kept as named lemmas. Equiv.traverse takes an applicative-valued function, so it is not a plain homomorphism with a standard bundle. I found no bundled object in the allowed sources that would cleanly package it. A grep for consumers found only Mathlib/Data/DList/Instances.lean, which uses Equiv.traversable and Equiv.isLawfulTraversable with DList.listEquivDList. That consumer already goes through the bundled instances, so a new bundle would have no concrete consumer. I found no justified finding. I did not look for a separate bundle of the maps t' α → t' β, such as a functor or natural-transformation structure.
